text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000211 bills 99215 far above its risk-adjusted expectation, but the small set of returned charts supports the billed levels, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 share persists after risk adjustment and shows up in every complexity stratum, most sharply among two-condition patients (28.6% vs 5.3% for all providers). The mix is also compressed toward the top, with no 99211 or 99212 and most claims at 99214, which favors upcoding. Against that, none of the documented 99213, 99214 or 99215 claims fell below the billed level, and there is no cloning signal from data-reviewed notes without lab lines. One low-complexity 99215 (C0110619, a single-condition depression patient) was documented at high MDM. The documentation evidence is thin, though: only 6 documented 99215 claims, and two of the supported examples (C0110619, C0110675) have no recorded minutes. That is too few to rule out a higher unsupported rate or notes written to match the billed level. A reviewer should first request charts for more 99215 claims, prioritizing the low-complexity sample (C0110564, C0110609, C0110649, C0110705, C0110706), and check whether the high-MDM notes reflect real problem complexity and risk or templated language."}
